---

This command helps you understand git.

First, check the status with `git status`.
Then, review changes with `git diff`.

If you want to commit, use !`git commit -m "$ARGUMENTS"`.

Remember: `git` is a version control tool.

Common commands:
- `git add .` - Stage all files
- `git log` - View history
- !`git push` - Push to remote

Use `npm install` for dependencies, then !`npm start` to run.
